title: Creating natural spoken audio · Level 2
slo: Describe the stages that convert written text into natural-sounding speech.

exercises.question_text: Which tasks belong to linguistic analysis? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Linguistic analysis looks up word pronunciations in lexicons. A lexicon is a pronunciation dictionary.
Linguistic analysis identifies syllables and their stress. This supplies pronunciation information for later stages.
Linguistic analysis maps normalized writing to phonemes. G2P supports this mapping for unfamiliar words.
Raw audio samples are made by a neural vocoder. Linguistic analysis determines pronunciation information first.
options.better_fit: Use neural vocoding after acoustic features have been created as mel-spectrograms.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Linguistic analysis prepares pronunciation details before audio generation.

exercises.question_text: Which tasks can recognition post-processing perform? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Post-processing can restore periods, commas, and question marks. This makes recognized words easier to read.
Post-processing can convert spoken number forms into formatted numbers. For example, it can format “one thousand twenty three” as “1,023.”
Capitalization is a post-processing task. It turns plain output into more readable writing.
Acoustic modeling predicts probabilities for phonemes from audio features. Post-processing happens after word decoding.
options.better_fit: Use phoneme probabilities when estimating likely speech sounds in audio frames.

exercises.explanation: Correct. These cleanup tasks improve the readability of recognized words.

exercises.question_text: A ___ turns mel-spectrograms into raw audio waveforms.

parts.text: turns mel-spectrograms into raw audio waveforms.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The audio would not reach the final waveform stage.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: MFCCs are recognition features and text normalizers prepare writing; a vocoder creates waveforms.

exercises.explanation: A neural vocoder converts acoustic features in a mel-spectrogram into raw audio waveforms.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the parts to form the correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The sentence no longer clearly shows when readability improvements occur.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Begin with decoded output, then show the formatting added to improve readability.

exercises.correct_answer: Decoded text gets punctuation and capitalization for easier reading
exercises.explanation: Punctuation and capitalization are applied after decoding to improve readability.

exercises.question_text: A navigation-app developer has phonemes and prosody targets ready, and acoustic feature generation has converted them into a mel-spectrogram. What should generate audible audio for the driver next?

options.rationale: A neural vocoder converts the resulting mel-spectrogram into raw audio waveforms. That produces audible directions.

options.error_type: Confuses letter-to-sound mapping with final audio generation
options.rationale: G2P maps letters to phonemes earlier in linguistic analysis. The phonemes are already ready here.
options.better_fit: Use G2P when written words still need pronunciation sounds.

feedback.intrinsic: The driver would wait while an already-complete mapping was repeated.
feedback.instructional: G2P comes before phonemes are ready; vocoding produces audible waveform audio.

options.error_type: Confuses recognition cleanup with speech creation
options.rationale: Punctuation restoration cleans recognition output. It does not create audio from synthesis features.
options.better_fit: Use punctuation restoration after recognition decoding.

feedback.intrinsic: The directions could be formatted as writing but remain silent.
feedback.instructional: A neural vocoder creates audible speech from synthesis representations.

options.error_type: Confuses recognition feature extraction with synthesis
options.rationale: MFCC extraction summarizes captured audio for recognition. It does not generate speech waveforms.
options.better_fit: Use MFCC extraction when preparing incoming audio for acoustic modeling.

feedback.intrinsic: The ready pronunciation information would not become an audio instruction.
feedback.instructional: MFCCs support recognition of incoming sound; vocoding synthesizes outgoing sound.

exercises.explanation: Correct. A neural vocoder generates waveform audio for the spoken directions.

exercises.question_text: A clinical professional dictates patient notes into an electronic health record. Some transcribed words may be uncertain, and a reviewer must check them. What should the system use?

options.rationale: Confidence scoring estimates certainty for recognized words. It can flag low-confidence words for human review.

options.error_type: Confuses TTS preparation with uncertainty checking
options.rationale: Text normalization expands written forms before speech is generated. It does not identify uncertain recognized words.
options.better_fit: Use text normalization when written dates, abbreviations, or symbols must be said aloud naturally.

feedback.intrinsic: A reviewer would not know which dictated words need closer checking.
feedback.instructional: Use confidence scores to direct review of recognition uncertainty.

options.error_type: Confuses word selection with review flags
options.rationale: Beam search helps choose a likely transcription during decoding. It does not provide review flags for uncertain words.
options.better_fit: Use beam search when selecting a likely transcription hypothesis.

feedback.instructional: Decoding selects a hypothesis; confidence scoring marks uncertainty in it.

options.error_type: Confuses audio features with transcript review
options.rationale: MFCC extraction creates compact audio features for recognition. It occurs before written words are reviewed.
options.better_fit: Use MFCC extraction to represent captured audio for acoustic modeling.

feedback.intrinsic: The reviewer would receive no cue about uncertainty.
feedback.instructional: MFCCs describe audio; confidence scores describe certainty in recognized words.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Confidence scores direct review to words that may need checking.

exercises.question_text: Put the pieces in the correct order.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The sentence would not clearly show what prosody predicts.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: State the prosody action, its values, then where they apply.

exercises.correct_answer: Prosody predicts pitch duration and energy for each phoneme
exercises.explanation: Prosody prediction produces pitch, duration, and energy values for each phoneme.

exercises.question_text: A learned system that maps an unfamiliar spelling to its speech sounds is called ___.

parts.text: A learned system that maps an unfamiliar spelling to its speech sounds is called

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: An unfamiliar spelling may be left without a sound mapping.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: A lexicon stores known pronunciations; neural G2P infers sounds from spelling patterns.

exercises.explanation: Neural G2P learns spelling-to-sound patterns, allowing it to infer pronunciations for unfamiliar names and uncommon words.

exercises.question_text: An e-learning designer hears that narrated lessons sound flat and robotic. Which prosody changes should the designer choose to make the speech more natural? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Pitch variation is part of prosody. Monotone prosody commonly makes speech sound robotic.
Pauses create natural rhythm and aid comprehension. They are a prosody element.
Stress and intensity can highlight important words. This makes delivery more expressive.
Expanding “Dr.” is text normalization. It does not address flat pitch, pauses, or emphasis.
options.better_fit: Use text normalization when an abbreviation must become a pronounceable word.

feedback.intrinsic: The lesson can remain monotone despite a correctly expanded abbreviation.
feedback.instructional: Address flat delivery with pitch, pauses, and stress.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Pitch variation, pauses, and emphasis make delivery more natural.

exercises.question_text: Before speech is generated, changing “@” into “at” is ___.

parts.text: Before speech is generated, changing “@” into “at” is

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The voice could attempt to handle a raw symbol.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Post-processing cleans recognition output, while G2P handles pronunciation after normalization.

exercises.explanation: Text normalization expands symbols into spoken forms before pronunciation.

exercises.question_text: A language-learning app needs to speak a learner’s uncommon name, but the name is not in its pronunciation dictionary. Which component should the developer use to choose its sounds?

options.rationale: Neural G2P learns spelling-to-sound patterns. It can handle uncommon names not found in a lexicon.

options.error_type: Confuses text expansion with unknown-word pronunciation
options.rationale: Text normalization expands forms such as symbols and dates. It does not choose phonemes for an unfamiliar name.
options.better_fit: Use text normalization when abbreviations, numbers, dates, or symbols need spoken forms.

feedback.intrinsic: The name could remain without a sound mapping.
feedback.instructional: An unknown name needs G2P to map spelling to phonemes.

options.rationale: Prosody prediction determines rhythm, pitch, and timing. It assumes the phoneme sequence is already known.
options.better_fit: Use prosody prediction after phonemes are available to decide delivery.

feedback.intrinsic: The name could receive expression without having basic sounds.
feedback.instructional: Determine phonemes with G2P before prosody shapes delivery.

options.error_type: Confuses pronunciation mapping with audio creation
options.rationale: Neural vocoding produces waveforms from mel-spectrograms. It does not map spelling to phonemes.
options.better_fit: Use neural vocoding to generate final audio after acoustic features are ready.

feedback.intrinsic: Audio production could begin before the name’s sounds were chosen.
feedback.instructional: G2P resolves spelling into sounds; vocoding creates audio.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Neural G2P can infer sounds for uncommon names.

exercises.question_text: A developer is building a voice assistant that reads financial notifications aloud. It must say “$25.50” naturally. Which text-normalization actions should the developer use? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Text normalization expands symbols into spoken forms. The dollar sign needs a word for natural speech.
Numbers are converted to spoken forms during normalization. This gives pronunciation stages speakable text.
Financial text can require specialized rules for currencies and percentages. These rules support an appropriate spoken form.

options.error_type: Confuses TTS preparation with recognition metadata
options.rationale: Word-level timestamps identify when recognized words occurred. They do not expand currency for speech.
options.better_fit: Use word timestamps to locate recognized words in recorded audio.

feedback.intrinsic: The notification could still be spoken awkwardly.
feedback.instructional: Currency pronunciation needs normalization of the symbol and number, not recognition timing metadata.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Currency symbols and values need spoken forms, and financial content can use specialized normalization rules.
